summary: Analyze diverged TPFanCtrl2 forks for features worth adopting

result.summary: Tinnci/TPFanCtrl2 (author shisoratsu) is a ground-up rewrite, not an incremental fork: starting 2025-12-22 it replaced the Win32 dialog app with an ImGui/Vulkan UI, an xmake build with GoogleTest, and a layered Core architecture (ECManager/FanController/SensorManager/ThermalManager with observer events), plus spdlog/std::format logging, JSON config, English/Chinese i18n, and PID closed-loop control with auto-tune. Nearly all 111 ahead-commits land in a Dec 22-25 2025 burst with two follow-up cleanups (Apr 5 and May 13, 2026). Because it is framework-heavy (Vulkan, ImGui, gtest, spdlog), almost nothing is portable as a diff to our deliberately tiny Win32 app — but two small control-loop ideas (fan tachometer stall recovery, per-sensor weights) are genuinely worth lifting as concepts.

notable.feature: Fan tachometer stall detection with command reapply
notable.detail: Each poll cycle, EvaluateFanFeedback() checks: if the commanded EC level is below 0x80 (i.e. a manual/smart level that should spin the fan) but fan1 tach reads under 300 RPM, a counter increments; after 3 consecutive low readings it logs 'Fan tachometer reports {} RPM at EC level 0x{:02X}; reapplying control command' and re-issues SetFanLevel() to recover from the EC silently dropping the command. Counter resets on healthy RPM or level >= 0x80. Our fork has the thermal fail-safe (force 0x40 over a temp threshold) and EC read-error fail-back to BIOS, but nothing that detects 'fan commanded but not spinning' and rewrites the fan register — this catches a different failure mode (lost/ignored EC write, fan stuck at 0 while temps climb).
notable.evidence: Commit 67f1014 'feat(thermal): enhance fan feedback evaluation and logging for RPM discrepancies' (https://github.com/Tinnci/TPFanCtrl2/commit/67f1014) — diff verified: new ThermalManager::EvaluateFanFeedback(), members m_fanNoSpinCounter, kFanMinOperationalRpm=300, kFanSpinRetryThreshold=3
notable.effort: ~30-60 lines in our existing poll loop (fanstuff.cpp): a counter, an RPM-vs-level check against the values we already read from EC offset 0x84, and a re-issue of the current fan level. No new files.

notable.feature: Per-sensor multiplicative weights (weighted sensor fusion)
notable.detail: Config keys SensorWeight1..16 (float, default 1.0) and SensorName1..16; the control temperature becomes Max(SensorTemp * SensorWeight). Documented rationale: Weight = GlobalTarget / SensorTarget, e.g. PID target 80C but battery should stay under 50C -> SensorWeight5=1.6, so the battery sensor effectively gets its own lower target across the whole curve. Our fork has additive offsets and ignore lists; a multiplicative weight is a different mechanism — an offset shifts a sensor by a constant, a weight rescales it so one sensor can have a proportionally stricter target at every smart-curve threshold. Same commit also added a 5-sample moving-average smoothing of temps (we already get jitter immunity from smart-curve hysteresis).
notable.evidence: Commits 9e823d7 'feat: Add sensor weight and name configurations to ConfigManager and SensorManager' (https://github.com/Tinnci/TPFanCtrl2/commit/9e823d7, includes TPFanCtrl2.ini doc: 'The final temperature used for control is Max(SensorTemp * SensorWeight)') and b4f9d2c 'feat: Enhance sensor management with custom naming, weighting, and safety features'
notable.effort: ~40-80 lines: INI parse for SensorWeightN next to our existing offset parsing, one multiply in the max-temp computation, optional display of the weighted value. Worth weighing against our existing offsets first — partial overlap in purpose.

notable.feature: .gitattributes for line-ending/diff hygiene
notable.detail: The fork carries a root .gitattributes (upstream-style). Per our own fork-vs-upstream audit, a missing .gitattributes is the single remaining hygiene gap in our repo; this fork demonstrates the file is the norm across the network.
notable.evidence: Root file listing of https://github.com/Tinnci/TPFanCtrl2 shows .gitattributes at repo root (file path: /.gitattributes)
notable.effort: 1 file, a few lines (text=auto plus binary entries for .lib/.ico/.exe).

notable.feature: PID closed-loop fan control with auto-tune and step-response preview
notable.detail: Alternative to threshold tables: FanController::UpdatePIDControl(float currentTemp, const PIDSettings&, float dt) with defaults Kp=0.5, Ki=0.01, Kd=0.1, integral and lastError state, mapped onto a minFan..maxFan range; UI adds PID parameter visualization, step-response preview, and auto-tune. Notably no anti-windup mechanism is visible in the implementation, which risks integral runaway during long thermal saturation. Not adoptable: it duplicates what our Smart curve editor already achieves, the auto-tune/preview is ImGui-bound, and the core impl has a known control-theory gap.
notable.evidence: Commits 7e29cfb 'Feat: Implement PID control for fan speed management...', cfe8fa3 'Feat: Add PID control settings and configuration saving functionality', 8b376ac 'feat: add PID step response preview and auto-tune functionality'; FanController.h (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tinnci/TPFanCtrl2/main/fancontrol/FanController.h) verified: m_integral, m_lastError, struct PIDSettings {Kp=0.5f, Ki=0.01f, Kd=0.1f}, no anti-windup
notable.effort: Core PID ~100-200 lines, but config/UI surface much larger; not recommended.

notable.feature: Full ImGui + Vulkan UI rewrite with i18n (EN/ZH)
notable.detail: Replaced the Win32 dialog UI entirely: ImGui rendered via Vulkan on a decoupled hardware thread, sidebar navigation, sensor-management table (custom names, weights, ignore toggles, live temps), theme system, Chinese/English translation manager, DPI scaling. This is the bulk of the 111 commits. Architecturally clean but the polar opposite of our no-framework Win32 approach — we already have dark mode, DPI-PerMonitorV2, sparkline, settings dialogs natively.
notable.evidence: Commit e6df032 'Implement modern ImGui GUI with Vulkan backend and decoupled hardware thread' (Dec 22 2025); c66d3f1 'Feat: Implement internationalization support with language selection and translation management'; repo description: 'A modern, high-performance fan control utility ... featuring an ImGui/Vulkan UI and smart PID control logic'
notable.effort: Not applicable (wholesale framework adoption).

notable.feature: EC access hardening (mutex, OBF drain, EC-type retry, write-verify)
notable.detail: ECManager wraps every EC transaction in a std::recursive_timed_mutex, drains the output buffer (OBF) before issuing commands to avoid stale-data corruption, probes two EC handshake types at init and switches-and-retries on timeout, and ToggleBitsWithVerify() reads back written values with up to 5 retries at 300ms. Solid, but functionally equivalent to the EC safety our fork already has (we meet/exceed upstream 2.3.3's EC/fan safety fixes, and our EC access is single-threaded by design so the mutex solves a problem we don't have).
notable.evidence: Commit 34d7dc3 'Modernize: Migrate low-level EC writes to FanController and ECManager, implement thread-safe locking'; ECManager.cpp content verified (recursive_timed_mutex lock_guard, drainObf lambda, 'timed out, switching EC type and retrying...', readback verify loop)
notable.effort: n/a — parity already.

notable.feature: 90C fail-safe that hands control back to BIOS (0x80)
notable.detail: Safety logic: if (maxTemp >= 90 && maxTemp < 128) fans->SetFanLevels(0x80, 0x80) — i.e. above 90C it forces BIOS auto mode rather than max fan. Our fail-safe forces 0x40 (full speed), which is the stronger guarantee on a P15G2 (BIOS auto can still be lazy); their variant is a design alternative, not an improvement to adopt.
notable.evidence: Commit b4f9d2c 'feat: Enhance sensor management with custom naming, weighting, and safety features' — quoted diff code: 'if (maxTemp >= 90 && maxTemp < 128) { fans->SetFanLevels(0x80, 0x80); // Force BIOS control }'
notable.effort: n/a — we have the stronger 0x40 fail-safe.

notable.feature: Fan2 auto-disable after repeated zero-RPM reads
notable.detail: Dual-fan robustness for unknown hardware: m_fan2ZeroCount with kFan2DisableThreshold=5 stops issuing fan2 commands after five consecutive 0-RPM readings (treats the machine as single-fan), with kFan1ActiveRpmThreshold=400 as the plausibility gate. Useful for a generic multi-model fork; wrong for ours — the P15G2 is known dual-fan, and silently ceasing fan2 commands would mask a dead fan instead of escalating, contradicting our fail-safe philosophy.
notable.evidence: fancontrol/FanController.h (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tinnci/TPFanCtrl2/main/fancontrol/FanController.h): 'm_fan2ZeroCount', 'static constexpr int kFan2DisableThreshold = 5', 'kFan1ActiveRpmThreshold = 400'; dual-fan support introduced in f0ea178 'feat(fancontrol): add dual fan support and related configuration options' and 950bc9a
notable.effort: n/a — undesirable for a machine-specific dual-fan fork.

notable.feature: Build/CI/test modernization: xmake, GoogleTest + mock IO, CodeQL/Dependabot//W4, dynamic git-tag versioning
notable.detail: Switched to xmake with GoogleTest integration and an IIOProvider/MockIOProvider seam so sensor/control logic is unit-testable without hardware; GitHub Actions split into ci.yml/release.yml with git-tag-derived versioning; CodeQL + Dependabot + /W4 enabled — though the fork itself later removed CodeQL ('ci: remove codeql workflow') after a long string of CI-fix commits. We already have build.yml/release.yml, an msbuild pipeline, a unit-test runner, and a warning-free build, so nothing here is a net gain; xmake/gtest would be bloat.

notable.feature: C++ modernization layer: spdlog/std::format logging, std::stop_token worker, JSON config, config caching
notable.detail: Logging unified onto spdlog with std::format and auto-flush; worker thread converted to cooperative cancellation via std::stop_token; ConfigManager gained JSON support alongside INI; Apr 2026 follow-up added config caching with an m_configChanged flag, simplified sensor retry to single-sample+retry, and fixed an ImGui render crash by seeding SmoothTemps. All dependency- or architecture-bound; our INI + lightweight logging (EM_REPLACESEL + in-memory tail) is intentionally smaller.
notable.evidence: Commits 65c44eb 'Refactor fancontrol to use std::format ... integrate spdlog for logging', 866f7f9 'refactor: Update WorkerThread to use std::stop_token for cooperative cancellation', ce78975 'feat: Add JSON support to ConfigManager and refactor application structure', 23165a5 'Core optimizations; UI crash fix; cleanup' (https://github.com/Tinnci/TPFanCtrl2/commit/23165a5, 28 files, +840/-5586)
notable.effort: n/a — dependency-driven; contrary to no-bloat goal.

result.summary: FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2 is the de-facto active maintenance fork of TPFanCtrl2; its author is also an upstream collaborator, so the 19-commits-ahead `main` branch differs from upstream by almost nothing (log-message wording, version strings 2.3.3->2.3.4, README model confirmations for P1 Gen7/Z16 Gen2, vcxproj SDK version) because the lid open/close feature developed here was merged upstream. The real fork-exclusive work lives on version branches 2.3.5-2.3.14, published as 'early beta' releases V2.3.5-V2.3.13-beta: power/suspend-aware fan-mode management (configurable LidClosedMode -> PowerSuspendMode, APM suspend/resume handling, Modern Standby S0 detection via Windows event-log subscription, 10s EC-access deferral after S0 resume), a SingleFan option, a fan ramp/hysteresis rework, and an EC port-autodetect/hardening pass in portio.cpp. Commit messages on these branches are mostly 'c'/'v', so the diffs (verified via a local clone of the fork's branches) are the real evidence.

notable.feature: Lid open/close automatic fan-mode switch
notable.detail: RegisterPowerSettingNotification(GUID_LIDSWITCH_STATE_CHANGE) + WM_POWERBROADCAST/PBT_POWERSETTINGCHANGE handler: on lid close save CurrentMode and switch to BIOS mode; on lid open restore the saved mode. Developed in this fork, later merged into upstream. Our fork already has the identical mechanism (fancontrol.x/fancontrol.cpp lines 46, 309, 3467-3490).
notable.effort: n/a - already present
notable.evidence: Commits https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/commit/70522be ("lid": adds DEFINE_GUID + RegisterPowerSettingNotification + WM_POWERBROADCAST handler) and https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/commit/8d4997f ("Fix previous mode": adds previousModeBeforeLidClose, restores it instead of hardcoded mode 2); 418455d ("fixup") removed a duplicate handler after upstream merge. Verified present in our tree at C:\Users\User00\Desktop\Open_Claude_session_2\TPFanCtrl2-main\fancontrol.x\fancontrol.cpp:3467-3490.

notable.feature: PowerSuspendMode: configurable lid/suspend fan behavior + APM suspend/resume handling
notable.detail: Ini parameter (evolved from LidClosedMode introduced on branch 2.3.5, misc.cpp:294 `LidClosedMode=` parse) selecting what happens on lid close AND on PBT_APMSUSPEND/PBT_APMRESUMEAUTOMATIC: 0=disabled, 1=BIOS mode (save+restore previous mode), 2=keep current mode, 3=manual mode + fans OFF (SetFan 0x00), 4=fans off on any suspend with 5s settle before restoring saved mode on resume. Our fork has zero WM_POWERBROADCAST suspend/resume handling (grep for PBT_APMSUSPEND/PBT_APMRESUME finds nothing) and our lid behavior is hardcoded to BIOS mode. Pure Win32, no frameworks. Relevant to our machine's thermal-trip history: today our app does nothing across sleep transitions.
notable.effort: ~100-150 lines across fancontrol.cpp (WM_POWERBROADCAST cases), fancontrol.h (savedMode/isPowerSuspendState members), misc.cpp (ini parse) + our Settings dialog
notable.evidence: Branch 2.3.12 head 34accb8 (https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/tree/2.3.12); verified diff origin/2.3.11..origin/2.3.12 in fancontrol/fancontrol.cpp shows PBT_APMSUSPEND -> savedMode=CurrentMode, PowerSuspendMode==4 -> SetFan(...,0x00), PBT_APMRESUMEAUTOMATIC -> Sleep(5000) + ModeToDialog(savedMode). Release notes https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/releases/tag/V2.3.12: "PowerSuspendMode ... (1) BIOS Mode ... (3) Manual Mode: switch to manual mode and turn off the fans (4) ... Turn fans off when suspend power events occur"; LidClosedMode parse verified at origin/2.3.5:fancontrol/misc.cpp:294.

notable.feature: Modern Standby (S0) entry/exit detection via Windows event-log subscription (ModernS0Mode)
notable.detail: Because Modern Standby does not deliver classic suspend messages reliably, the fork subscribes with EvtSubscribe (wevtapi.lib) to the System channel query *[System[Provider[@Name='Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Power'] and (EventID=506 or EventID=507)]] (506=S0 entry, 507=exit). A static EventLogCallback renders the event XML (EvtRender), string-searches the EventID, and on entry saves CurrentMode and applies ModernS0Mode (0=disabled default, 1=BIOS, 2=keep, 3=manual+fans off); on exit restores the saved mode. Plain Win32 API, ~120 lines, fits a tiny app. Our P15G2 is a Modern Standby machine and our fork has no S0 awareness at all (grep ModernS0/GUID_CONSOLE_DISPLAY_STATE: no matches). Caution when porting: the callback runs on an EvtSubscribe worker thread, so EC writes must go through our existing EC mutex, and blocking Sleeps in the callback should be avoided/marshalled to the UI thread.
notable.effort: ~120-150 lines in fancontrol.cpp/.h + misc.cpp ini parse + link wevtapi.lib
notable.evidence: Branch 2.3.12 head 34accb8 (https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/tree/2.3.12); verified diff origin/2.3.11..origin/2.3.12 adds #include <winevt.h>, #pragma comment(lib, "wevtapi.lib"), EvtSubscribe call with the quoted Kernel-Power 506/507 query, FANCONTROL::EventLogCallback and HandleModernStandbyEvent with "Detected Modern S0 Entry"/"Exit" traces. Release notes https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/releases/tag/V2.3.12: "Monitor 'Modern S0' events in a similar fashion as Lid Open/Close events".

notable.feature: 10-second EC access deferral after Modern S0 exit
notable.detail: On detecting Modern S0 exit (Kernel-Power EventID 507) the app traces "Detected Modern S0 Exit, defer access to EC (10s)" and Sleep(10000) before touching the EC, because the embedded controller can return garbage or NAK right after resume. A tiny safety guard squarely in our fork's safety-guard theme; we have no resume-side EC guard. (Implementation caveat: their Sleep blocks the event callback thread - we would gate our poll timer instead.)
notable.effort: ~5-15 lines once S0 detection (item above) exists
notable.evidence: Branch 2.3.13 head e886f05 (https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/tree/2.3.13), verified in tree at origin/2.3.13:fancontrol/fancontrol.cpp:440-441: `this->Trace("Detected Modern S0 Exit, defer access to EC (10s)"); ::Sleep(10000);`. Release V2.3.13-beta notes: "10s delay before accessing EC when coming out of Modern S0".

notable.detail: Ini flag parsed in misc.cpp (`SingleFan=`); when set, SetFan skips the fan2 select/write/verify sequence (fan2_ok forced true) and the version string becomes "Dual/Single Fan". Broadens device compatibility for the fork's general audience. Irrelevant to our purpose-built dual-fan P15G2 fork.

notable.evidence: Commit 3586df26023e29eeaf85eb83c854b0bb3c192e51 "SingleFan option" (branch 2.3.7, https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/tree/2.3.7): verified diff adds `SingleFan = false` member, misc.cpp `_strnicmp(buf, "SingleFan=", 10)` parse, fanstuff.cpp `if (!SingleFan)` guard around fan2 writes. notable.feature: Smart fan-curve ramp up/down + hysteresis rework
notable.detail: Replaces upstream's stateful "hyst zone" check (LastSmartLevel anchor compared against newLevel.temp +/- hyst) by folding hysteresis directly into level selection: ramp-up requires MaxTemp >= level.temp + hystUp, ramp-down requires MaxTemp <= level.temp - hystDown; commit 743bd80 then removes LastSmartLevel entirely. Cleaner and removes the documented foot-gun "DO NOT HAVE HYSTERESIS OVERLAP WITH FAN TEMPS IN CONFIG!". Not adoptable: our fork already has its own ramp-up/ramp-down + hysteresis algorithm with a LastSmartLevel anchor and dedicated unit tests (fancontrol.x/fanstuff.cpp:430-471 referencing tests/fanlogic_tests.cpp); swapping algorithms would discard tested behavior for no functional gain.
notable.effort: ~60 lines in fanstuff.cpp if ever wanted
notable.evidence: Commits aca7d516947a6e822acc769aede953320aa2af2c "Improve Ramp Up/Down logic" (branch 2.3.8) and 743bd80db720d7b7fe7ae4a2aca05d8b204dfb02 "Remove lastSmartLevel" (branch 2.3.9 head); diffs verified locally showing `this->SmartLevels[i].temp + this->SmartLevels[i].hystUp` ramp-up and `- hystDown` ramp-down conditions. Release notes V2.3.8 "Improved fan ramp up and ramp down control logic", V2.3.9 "Quick fix improving hysteresis handling". Our equivalent: C:\Users\User00\Desktop\Open_Claude_session_2\TPFanCtrl2-main\fancontrol.x\fanstuff.cpp:430-471.

notable.feature: EC port-layout auto-detection and EC access hardening (portio.cpp rework)
notable.detail: Net +363/-96 in portio.cpp: documents the ACPI EC command set with spec links, defines an EC_PORT_LAYOUTS table {0x1604/0x1600 "ACPI_EC_TYPE1", 0x66/0x62 "ACPI_EC_TYPE2"} and "attempts to auto-detect which port layout is present by trying one, then the other if the first fails", adds BURST/SCI_EVT/SMI_EVT status-bit constants, RECOVERY_DRAIN_READS=8 recovery-drain logic, and a STRICT_EC_READ_OBF_HANDLING switch. Notably risky: their own V2.3.10 with this rework was "superseded due to reported issues with embedded controller access changes" and refined in 2.3.11. Not adoptable: our fork targets one fixed machine (P15G2, known EC ports) and our prior analysis found porting EC-layer changes regresses our hardened implementation.
notable.effort: ~400 lines, 1 file
notable.evidence: Verified local diff origin/2.3.9..origin/2.3.10..origin/2.3.11 (branch heads 743bd80 -> 6853879 -> 7c46d06, https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/tree/2.3.11), fancontrol/portio.cpp net +363/-96 with quoted comment "This code attempts to auto-detect which port layout is present by trying one, then the other if the first fails." Release notes V2.3.10/V2.3.11 at https://github.com/FanDjango/TPFanCtrl2/releases confirm the supersession.

notable.detail: Refactors SetFan to a new `bool PollECByte(char offset, char* out, int expected, int timeoutMs)` that polls the EC fan register until it reads back the expected value (200ms timeout) instead of fixed Sleep(100) read-verify, cuts the retry backoff 300ms->100ms, and fixes a latent upstream bug where `source == "Smart"` compared pointers instead of strings. result.summary: ghubliming/TPFanCtrl2_P16s is a config-and-binary repackaging of upstream TPFanCtrl2 (forked at upstream 2.2.1, commit 02761cf) for the ThinkPad P16s. result.summary: withmorten/TPFanCtrl2 is a small personal fork, 4 commits ahead of upstream (Dec 2025 - Jan 2026), all by withmorten, focused on manual-fan-mode quality of life. It adds two-way Manual/Smart hysteresis (auto-exit Manual on high temp, auto-return when cool again), de-hardcodes several behaviors into config keys (exit target mode, lid-close handling, Fahrenheit), filters a bogus 0x77 EC sensor reading, and consolidates the duplicated stay-on-top dialog template into one template with a runtime WS_EX_TOPMOST toggle.

notable.feature: Manual-mode hysteresis: auto-return to Manual when temp drops (ManModeEntryLo) + configurable exit target mode (ManModeExitModeLo)
notable.detail: Upstream/our fork only has one-way ManModeExit: Manual(3) -> Smart(2) when MaxTemp exceeds threshold (our fancontrol.cpp:3174-3177 hardcodes ModeToDialog(2)). The fork adds the return path and makes the exit target configurable. Verified final code in fork's fanstuff.cpp: `if (CurrentMode == 3 && ManModeExitLo && MaxTemp > ManModeExitLoInternal) CurrentMode = ManModeExitModeLo; else if (CurrentMode == ManModeExitModeLo && ManModeEntryLo && MaxTemp <= ManModeEntryLoInternal) CurrentMode = 3;`. Both branches gated on the config key being nonzero (defaults: ManModeExitModeLo=2, ManModeEntryLo=80); Fahrenheit/Celsius conversion handled like ManModeExit. Caveat if porting: re-entry fires whenever CurrentMode equals the exit-target mode and temp is low - it does not track whether the exit actually happened, so a user who manually selects Smart gets pulled into Manual once cool. notable.feature: Process watchdog via Windows Task Scheduler (TPFC_Task_Monitor_Create.ps1)
notable.detail: 357-line PowerShell installer that generates a sidecar monitor script (TPFC_Monitor.ps1) and registers a scheduled task to run it. Parameters: ProcessName (default TPFanControl), MaxRetries (2), RetryDelaySeconds (5), CheckIntervalMinutes (1). The generated monitor checks whether TPFanControl.exe is running, retries with delay, relaunches it if dead, logs with timestamps to a temp file, and shows a Windows Forms error popup on failure. Task registration uses Register-ScheduledTask cmdlets (logon trigger + repeating interval trigger, SYSTEM/highest privileges, auto-restart 3x) with a schtasks+XML fallback. Addresses a gap our fork has: if our app crashes while holding a manual EC fan level, nothing restarts it, and EC control stays stale until the firmware watchdog times out. Caveats if adopting: running the task as SYSTEM at highest privileges means the relaunched GUI may land in the wrong session/without the user's settings dir, and the same goal can be met with a much simpler per-user scheduled task; consider rewriting as a ~40-line script or task XML rather than porting verbatim.

notable.feature: SecWinUptime boot-delay logic defeated by Windows Fast Startup
notable.detail: Upstream-documented flaw: SecWinUptime/SecStartDelay compares tick-count uptime, but 'this uptime IS NOT set to zero by a power off shutdown' when Fast Startup is enabled (power-on is a kernel-hibernation resume), so the EC-settling start delay is silently skipped on most real power-ons. Our fork has the identical logic on GetTickCount64 (fancontrol.cpp:428-460). Upstream's resolution is documentation (disable Fast Startup / shift+shutdown). Minimal adoption: add the caveat to TPFanControl.ini comments and README; optional code fix would compare wall-clock now minus real boot time instead of tick count.
notable.effort: doc-only (a few ini/README lines); optional ~20-line code alternative
